why: A national gym market of about $24 billion today, with boutique studios at $2 billion growing faster than full-service and budget gyms, is believable.
Each hotel's revenue split adds to 100%, and city-centre hotels earning $17 to $53 million a year at 66% to 89% occupancy are believable.
The eight revenue sources add to the stated $7.6 billion total, a believable size for a media group with print, broadcast and digital arms.
A nine-office recruitment agency earning $17 to $42 million in fees per office while spending $1 to $4 million on job boards is believable.
The waterfall adds up ($3.10 + $1.15 = $4.25, + $0.85 = $5.10, + $2.12 = $7.22), and green coffee at about $3 to $5 per kg with a 20% roasting weight loss is believable.
Data prices of $3 to $4.50 per GB with use falling from 25 to 10 GB a month as price rises is a stylised but possible demand picture for a mobile operator.
Each campus's income split adds to 100%, and a private university campus with $49 to $212 million of income, 15% to 35% from government, is believable.
A regional bottled water market of $640 million, with Aquavel holding 1% to 6% of each region's market, is believable.
Software sales teams signing $7 to $17 million of new contracts a year at a cost of $1 to $3 million each are believable.
The cost lines sit within the totals, and an error-prone outside labeller whose mistakes cost $41,500 to fix across 96 batches (about $430 a batch) is possible.
